subject: chemistry
title: Brønsted-Lowry acids and bases
key_idea: A Brønsted-Lowry acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor. Acid-base reactions are proton transfers, and each acid has a conjugate base that differs by one H⁺.

blocks.text: This section defines acids and bases by what happens to protons. A proton here is an H⁺ ion.

items.meaning: A species that donates a proton (H⁺).
A species that accepts a proton (H⁺).
A reaction in which a proton is transferred from an acid to a base.

items: A base needs a lone pair of electrons to bond to the proton it accepts.
In water, an acid HA donates H⁺ to H₂O and forms H₃O⁺ ions. This is usually written as H⁺(aq).
Water can act as an acid or as a base, depending on what it reacts with.
Acid-base reactions in solution are usually **equilibria**, because the proton transfer can go in both directions.

blocks.label: An acid in water
where: HA = the acid, which donates H⁺
H₂O = the base, which accepts H⁺

blocks.label: A base in water
where: NH₃ = the base, which accepts H⁺
H₂O = the acid, which donates H⁺

items: An acid donates a proton. A base accepts a proton.
Every acid-base reaction is a transfer of H⁺.
In water, H₂O acts as a base with acids and as an acid with bases.

blocks.text: Every acid-base equilibrium contains two conjugate pairs. This section shows how to find them.

items.meaning: What is left when an acid has donated a proton.
What is formed when a base has accepted a proton.
Two species that differ by one H⁺.

items: Find the species that loses H⁺: that is the acid. Its partner on the other side is its conjugate base.
Find the species that gains H⁺: that is the base. Its partner on the other side is its conjugate acid.
The acid in each pair has one more H⁺ than its base, so its charge is one unit more positive.

blocks.text: In CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺, the pairs are CH₃COOH / CH₃COO⁻ and H₃O⁺ / H₂O.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Sort the species in the ethanoic acid equilibrium into acids and bases.
diagram.prompt: In CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺, sort each species by its role in the direction given.

items: Conjugate pairs differ by one H⁺.
An acid-base equilibrium has two conjugate pairs.
A species can be an acid in one pair and a base in another, as water is.

blocks.text: The role of H⁺ in the reactions of acids
Acids show their reactions through H⁺(aq). Ionic equations leave out the spectator ions.

items: With a metal, H⁺ is **reduced** to H₂ and the metal is oxidised.
With an oxide, alkali or carbonate, H⁺ is the proton donor and the oxide, hydroxide or carbonate ion is the proton acceptor.
